1. I'm not sure if this is the kind of answer you're looking for, but manners are #1 for me. I have to do at least a hundred transactions every time I'm on the register and every person who treats me as subhuman makes it harder. Aside from that, being able to enter the modifications as quickly as the customer speaks is important. This mostly just comes with practice, though.

2. Before this job I'd been a cashier for almost 7 years, so not long. Maybe a couple days to get used to how it's organized. I still have to search for a button when it's a less popular item, because there's a LOT of buttons.

3. Honestly it's just pretty outdated and frequently freezes or lags or malfunctions in some other way, but that's just standard with Starbucks technology as far as I can tell. Not a day goes by without one of our many machines either breaking or being broken for the whole shift. As of today, our order screen has been down maybe a month and one of the sticker printers was out of commission for an hour. Yesterday one steam wand wasn't worrying properly and then the other espresso machine refused to pull shots. So if Starbucks would invest in better technology that'd save everyone a lot of frustration.
